description:
We are an innovative team tackling the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge! We focus on rapid, AI-assisted prototyping and interactive web solutions to design engaging space training modules.

What we bring: Passion for space tech, Python and web basics, and a structured, step-by-step approach to turning ideas into working prototypes fast.
summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive educational simulation that introduces students to the challenges of sustaining human life in space. Players take the role of a mission commander and manage a four-person crew at a simulated Moon or Mars outpost for 30 days. They monitor oxygen, water, food, electrical power, and radiation protection while choosing engineering operations and responding to unexpected emergencies. The simulation encourages resource management, critical thinking, and understanding of space-habitat systems. It is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and runs directly in a web browser without requiring installation. The project is an independent educational prototype, not an official NASA application.
details:
Project Overview

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive browser-based simulation designed to introduce students to the challenges of long-duration human space exploration.

How It Works

Players choose between a Mars Outpost and a Lunar Research Base, select a difficulty level, and take command of a four-person astronaut crew. Their objective is to maintain essential habitat systems and survive a 30-day mission.

The simulation includes five resource indicators: oxygen, water, food, electrical power, and radiation protection. Players can perform six engineering operations, including oxygen production, water recycling, greenhouse food production, power generation, radiation shielding, and research.

Unexpected emergencies challenge players to make decisions while managing limited resources.

Technology Used

  • HTML5
  • CSS3
  • JavaScript
  • Responsive web design

The application runs directly in a modern browser without requiring a backend or external software installation.

Educational Impact

The project introduces systems thinking, resource management, engineering decisions, and the importance of life-support systems during space exploration.

NASA Connection

The project's educational concepts are informed by NASA research on Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS), deep-space habitation, water recovery, oxygen generation, and radiation protection.

The numerical values and mission events are simplified illustrative game mechanics, not actual NASA engineering specifications.

AI Assistance Disclosure

AI assistance was used to review and improve the JavaScript code, refine the project description, improve interface presentation, and prepare the demonstration slides. The final project should be reviewed and validated by the team before submission.

This is an independent educational project and is not an official NASA application.
